idea: Invoicing and late-payment reminders for freelance designers in the US

strategist.problem: A freelance designer in the US sends an invoice, waits 30+ days past terms, and manually chases the client over email while cash flow stalls and awkwardness builds.
strategist.target_customer: US-based freelance graphic/UI designers billing $3k–$15k/month to 3–10 retainer clients, who feel the pain the day an invoice crosses its due date unpaid.
strategist.mission: Automate invoice follow-up and late-payment chasing so freelance designers get paid on time without awkward client emails.

competitors.name: FreshBooks
competitors.differentiator: We are purpose-built for designer freelancers' reminder cadence, not a full small-business accounting suite they'd pay more for.

competitors.name: Wave (free invoicing)
competitors.differentiator: Wave sends generic reminders; we win with designer-tuned, escalating, tone-matched chase sequences.

competitors.name: Stripe Invoicing
competitors.differentiator: Stripe handles payment rails but lacks friendly multi-step relationship-aware chasing freelancers actually want.

scope_cuts: Skip time tracking, expense management, and full double-entry accounting — we only do invoicing plus reminders.
Skip a native mobile app at launch; responsive web app covers the invoice-send-and-chase workflow.
Skip multi-currency and non-US tax logic at launch; US-only, USD-only to ship in 2-4 weeks.

stack.name: Next.js
stack.why: App Router + Server Actions handle invoice pages, reminder scheduling cron, and Stripe webhooks in one deployable app.

stack.name: Supabase
stack.why: Postgres stores invoices, clients, and reminder sequences; built-in auth covers designer sign-in without a separate auth service.

stack.name: Tailwind CSS
stack.why: Invoice and dashboard UI ships fast with utility classes; designer-facing product needs clean visuals without a component library tax.

stack.name: Cloudflare Pages
stack.why: Free tier hosts the commercial Next.js app legally, unlike Vercel Hobby; Workers cron can trigger reminder emails.

stack.name: Resend
stack.why: Transactional email API sends invoice and escalating late-reminder emails with open tracking; free tier covers launch volume.

stack.name: Stripe
stack.why: Collects the USD subscription via Checkout and Billing; 2.9% + $0.30 US card fee is the standard rail.

ai_tools.name: Claude
ai_tools.why: Claude Code writes the Next.js + Supabase invoice and reminder-cron codebase in the 2-4 week window.

ai_tools.name: Cursor
ai_tools.why: AI code editor for iterating invoice UI and reminder-sequence screens alongside Claude Code.

ai_tools.name: OpenAI API
ai_tools.why: gpt-6-luna drafts tone-matched escalating reminder email copy per client relationship at $0.10/$0.50 per 1M tokens.

ai_tools.name: v0
ai_tools.why: Generates the invoice form and dashboard UI components quickly before hand-writing them in Next.js.

mvp_features: Create and send a USD invoice with Net-15/Net-30 terms, then auto-send an escalating 3-step late-reminder sequence (day 1, 7, 14 past due) with tone-matched copy the designer approves before each send.
Client dashboard showing every unpaid invoice, days overdue, and the next scheduled reminder with one-click pause or manual nudge.
Stripe Checkout subscription gate: free for 3 invoices, then paywall the reminder automation behind the monthly plan.

first_10_steps: Register a .com domain at $1/mo via Cloudflare Registrar and point nameservers to Cloudflare.
Run npx create-next-app@latest with TypeScript, Tailwind, App Router in a new repo.
Create a Supabase project; run SQL migrations for clients, invoices, reminder_events, subscriptions tables.
Scaffold auth with Clerk; gate /dashboard behind sign-in.
Build the invoice create/send flow: USD amount, Net-15/30 terms, PDF or hosted invoice link emailed via Resend.
Implement a Cloudflare Workers cron (daily 6am ET) that queries overdue invoices and enqueues reminder emails at day 1/7/14 past due.
Call OpenAI gpt-6-luna to draft each reminder's body with tone presets (friendly, firm, final), queued for designer approval in-app.
Wire Stripe Checkout + Billing webhook to flip accounts from free (3 invoices) to subscribed, unlocking automated reminders.
Deploy to Cloudflare Pages, connect domain, verify Resend domain SPF/DKIM, send 10 test invoices end-to-end.
Record a 90-second Loom-style demo with Claude Code + HyperFrames showing an invoice going overdue and reminders firing.

pricing.name: Free
features: Create and send up to 3 invoices per month

revenue_targets.notes: Founding designers from Dribbble and Twitter

key_assumptions: US freelance designers will pay $19/month to avoid awkward late-payment emails.
5 paying customers can be acquired in 30 days via direct outreach on Dribbble and Twitter.
OpenAI API costs remain negligible at launch volume under $1/month.
Marketing spend of $100/month yields 3-5 new paying customers per month.

channels.name: Dribbble + X designer DMs
channels.tactic: Send 30 DMs/day (15 on Dribbble to US freelance designers posting client work, 15 on X to designers complaining about late payments) with a free overdue-invoice audit of their last invoice.

channels.name: r/freelance and r/graphic_design Reddit
channels.tactic: Comment daily on 10 threads about late payments with a concrete reminder-email teardown, then DM the 5 most frustrated posters offering to draft their next chase sequence free.

first_10_customers: Day 1-3: Search Dribbble for US designers with 'available for work' tags; DM 30/day offering to write their next overdue-invoice chase email free, no signup required.
Day 4-7: Post 5 overdue-invoice email teardowns on X tagging the designer who shared the invoice; reply daily to 10 'client hasn't paid' tweets with the 3-step sequence.
Day 8-12: Sort r/freelance and r/graphic_design by 'late payment' flair; comment on 10 threads/day, DM the 5 angriest posters with a free reminder-sequence draft.
Day 13-18: Join 3 Dribbble Slack/Discord servers for freelance designers; answer every 'invoice' or 'unpaid' message within 1 hour, DM the asker a free audit.
Day 19-24: Offer the first 10 designers 3 months of Pro free in exchange for a 15-minute call where they set up their first invoice live on Zoom.
Day 25-30: Ask each of the 10 for 1 named designer referral; DM the referral the same free overdue-invoice audit offer.
growth.cold_message: Saw your post about a client ghosting your invoice — I built a tool that sends day 1/7/14 escalating reminders so you never send that awkward email. Want me to draft the 3-step chase sequence for your current overdue invoice, free, no signup? Reply and I'll send it in 10 minutes.

objections.objection: "I can just set calendar reminders and email clients myself."
objections.response: You can — this is for the 2am 'did they see it?' spiral. Try it free on your next 3 invoices; if the first reminder doesn't go out, you've lost nothing.
Those send one generic nudge. Show me your last 3 overdue invoices and I'll draft the tone-matched 3-step sequence for each — free, whether or not you sign up.

critic.verdict: The plan is a coherent bootstrapped SaaS for US freelance designers with a clear problem, realistic $19 pricing, and channels that fit a solo founder's constraints. The build stack, free-tier tooling, and 2-4 week ship window all respect the hard rules. The main uncertainty is whether direct DM outreach converts fast enough to hit 5 paying customers in 30 days.
critic.biggest_risk: Cold DMs to designers on Dribbble/X converting to paid subscriptions at the assumed rate — cold outreach to creative professionals typically converts far below 1-2%, so 5 paying customers in 30 days may not materialize.
